Definition: from G2596 and a derivative of G739; to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust:--fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.
BiblicalUsage: To complete thoroughly is to mend and restore, and Jesus saw James and John mending their nets, and Paul tells the spiritual to restore the fallen in meekness, and Hebrews prays that God would make us perfect in every good work. Peter says the God of all grace will make us perfect, stablish, strengthen, and settle us after we have suffered. The word holds the net, the brother, and the saint together: all are mended by the same hands.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God mends what is broken, whether it is a net, a brother, or my own heart. I hold that restoration is His work and His promise, and suffering is not the end of it but the way through it.
